findings.text: blocking: settle_run_scratch removes from worker_scratch_root() while it reads live pointers and run directories from RECKON_HOME, and it omits the coherence guard garbage_collect_orphan_scratch applies at gc.py:1044-1052 ("state and scratch roots differ"): a caller that sets RECKON_HOME without RECKON_WORKER_SCRATCH_ROOT therefore sees the host-wide /tmp/reckon-crew-scratch with no live pointer for the runs that are actually live in the operator's real home, and rmtree's their run-named copies at once when a run directory in the private home records an end, or after SCRATCH_GRACE_SECONDS otherwise. _scratch_process_holders only protects a process whose cwd or fd is inside the directory, so a worker between turns (cwd in its worktree) is not protected. This is the destructive-mis-scope class the sibling pass already guards against.

non-blocking: _write_release_receipt writes the receipt with target.write_text(json.dumps(...)), which is neither atomic nor mode-restricted, instead of the repository's owner for a JSON record write, reckon/_store.py:607 write_json_atomically (used by promotion_scope._append_landing_record for landing.json and by runs._write_json for pointer and claim records). The very durability the receipt exists for is lost: a crash mid-write leaves a truncated release.json that a later reader cannot parse, while the owner's tmp-then-rename cannot.

non-blocking: the done-when requires a case that drives a review promotion through the named route and shows the scratch left with no release block at the base and removed with a release block at the head; the landed cases call release_module._release_after_promotion directly (:263, :284) and monkeypatch _commit_landing_writes to raise (:292), so no test drives promotion.complete for a review record and neither arm is shown red at the base. The mechanism is covered at the release-function boundary, not through the route the done-when names.

non-blocking: the done-when requires the fragment to name the route of each of the four unexplained survivors; route-d names two runs and says the other two were reclaimed (:80) without naming them or their records, so a reader cannot check the class against four individuals. The route class is named; two of the four plan-named survivors are not.
